blind_target.authors: Bertram L, Schjeide BM, Hooli B, Mullin K, Hiltunen M, Soininen H, Ingelsson M, Lannfelt L, Blacker D, Tanzi RE
blind_target.title: No association between CALHM1 and Alzheimer’s disease risk.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Several independent research groups have observed
that P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the

AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]. These

observations reinforce a hypothetical recessive model

for the P86L variant in AD. So, we decided to evalu-

ate this model in AAO in Spanish AD patients.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
We have provided new evidence for the role of the

CALHM1P86L marker in ADrisk. Infact,wehaveob-

served a trend toward association in case-control stud-

ies and a full independent replication of the P86L ef-

fect in AAO. Intriguingly, both results are evidentonly

when EOAD patients are eliminated from the pool and

when a recessive model is applied to analyses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Outcome follows the explicit comparisons; the disease-risk nulls of prior replication papers are not themselves the age-at-onset claims re-tested here.

prior_decision.quote: Unfortunately, original ﬁndings, obtained in ﬁve different case-control series, were not replicated in a large-scale study of familial AD [2] and in six additional studies conducted in AD patients and controls from different populations (Sweden [2], Finland [2], Belgium [3], Caucasian Americans [4,5], and Asians [6]).
prior_decision.reason: Wrong original / non-target prior replication study. Reference [2] (Bertram et al., 2008, including the original authors' reply in Cell 135: 993-996) is explicitly introduced as an earlier replication study of the original findings [1] and included in the meta-analysis; its mention alongside [1, 4, 11] in Results serves to motivate testing [1]'s P86L variant under a recessive model for age at onset rather than establishing an independent replication target omitted by the shipped data.

blind_target.outcome_reasoning: New Spanish sample tests the published CALHM1 association and age-at-onset findings. The dominant versus recessive contrast makes the first target mixed; age-at-onset replication supports the remaining targets. Li includes other CALHM1 markers, leaving some target specificity uncertainty.

prior_decision.quote: Several independent research groups have observed that P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]. These observations reinforce a hypothetical recessive model for the P86L variant in AD. So, we decided to evaluate this model in AAO in Spanish AD patients.
prior_decision.reason: Wrong original / background citation. Reference [11] (Li et al., 2008) is cited only once in passing as part of the background observation that 'P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]' to motivate evaluating the recessive model for P86L in the authors' replication of [1]; the present paper only genotyped P86L and P85P and did not re-test Li et al.'s GWAS candidate SNPs.
